key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap versus narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so the evaporation recipe must be tuned to the target bandgap.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a practical design rule for fabricating solvent-free all-perovskite tandem absorbers with controlled bandgaps and improved device stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare solid-state conversion in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Use guided absorber design to build and test an evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell
evidence_signal: The study reports bandgaps spanning 1.26–1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem efficiency of 19.2%, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Absolute precursor thickness and vertical compositional gradients strongly affect final phase formation, so process control and reproducibility are critical.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
